items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Lester Young had been . . . drank so much brandy... played a real lazy slow solo which is a classic.

ctx.x: You recorded in a thing that’s recently been reissued on video and CD . . . that’s being widely discussed again, in The Sound of Jazz, which had Billie Holiday, Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, and many many other legendary jazz figures.

Yeah, all of them dying, most of them. Drank their self or doped their self to death. Billie was dying then. Just skin and bones. Lester Young had been . . . drank so much brandy, ’til his eyes . . . You can see that their eyes look like two . . . something in a bowl . . . look like two eggs in a bowl of milk. Eyes that lost their pupils, he was so drunk. Had to lead him. In that solo you see Lester take with Billie, they had to lead him . . . pick him up, almost, and lead him to the bandstand. When they brought…

Then you recorded with quite a few other people, most recently, in recent years, Wynton Marsalis. What was it like recording with such a wide range of people, going from some of the early jazz pioneers to some of the latest up and coming . . .

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: His father was a musician. He gave me an old picture. It’s got Willie Humphrey when he was about 17 in it. They’re playing in a yard. I’m not sure what his father played. It was either trumpet or violin, something like that. Valto. How did you . . . When you came up as a kid, what kind of life did you have? Where did you go to school?
I went to Medard school. I went to private school from kindergarten . . . not kindergarten . . . from first grade through the second grade.
